name: Collaborative robots and autonomous mobile robots
summary: Flexible robot arms and mobile robots assist with handling, transport and repetitive work in factories and warehouses.
useCase: An autonomous mobile robot brings parts to a workcell, while a collaborative arm performs a repetitive loading task under a validated safety setup.
whyNow: Robots can address repetitive work and improve throughput when the surrounding process is well designed. Amazon’s disclosures illustrate scale: 350,000 robotic drive units in 2021, 750,000 mobile robots in 2023 and one million robots of all types in 2025. Those changing definitions must be kept visible. Meanwhile, A3’s 2026 order data shows a real commercial market for collaborative robots alongside conventional automation.

mainstream.scope: A routine procurement option for medium-to-large warehouses and flexible manufacturing tasks with a clear automation case.
mainstream.rationale: Mature suppliers, deployed fleets and established integration practices support the window. Mainstream means a normal option for suitable tasks, not robots at every small factory. Integration, workflow variability and safety assessment can dominate the hardware cost. Growth should be evaluated by productive installations rather than vendor demonstrations.

metric.name: Amazon disclosed robot fleet — company scale proxy
metric.scope: Amazon operations; company categories broaden over time.
metric.growthLabel: Scale milestones: >350k drive units → 1m robots of all types
metric.limitations: One highly automated operator, not the global AMR or cobot installed base. Definitions change from drive units to mobile robots to all robots, so no growth percentage or CAGR is calculated. Fleet size is not equivalent to labor savings or productive hours.
metric.futureNote: No directly comparable public fleet forecast is used. Growth depends on integration economics, reliability and deployment beyond the largest operators.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: Amazon reported more than 350,000 robotic drive units in its operations.
Amazon reported more than 520,000 drive units and introduced Proteus.
Amazon described a fleet of more than 750,000 mobile robots.
IFR reported that collaborative robots represented 10.5% of 2023 industrial installations; this is a lagged statistic.
Amazon deployed its millionth robot; the count now includes more than mobile drive units.
A3 reported 2,774 collaborative robots ordered in North America in H1, separate from the global installed base.

tailwinds: Labor availability, ergonomic tasks and variable production favor flexible automation.
Improved perception and orchestration make more workflows technically feasible.
bottlenecks: Integration, site preparation and exceptions frequently cost more than the robot itself.
Collaborative hardware still requires a task-specific risk assessment; not every application can run safely without barriers.
watchMetrics: Paid production deployments, utilization and payback including integration and support.
Interventions per operating hour, throughput, availability and renewal/expansion in robot-as-a-service fleets.
